ai.description: This gecko reaches 60–70 mm SVL. It is brownish-grey with dark transverse dorsal bands and a distinct nuchal collar. Key features include a slender body, granular scales, and a precloacal groove.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus deccanensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark, V-shaped marking on the nape and a series of dark, wavy transverse bands on the back.
ai.habitat: *Cyrtodactylus deccanensis* inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests of the Northern Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: *Cyrtodactylus deccanensis* is a strictly nocturnal gecko that spends its nights actively foraging for small insects along rocky outcrops and tree trunks.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cyrtodactylus deccanensis* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between June and September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus deccanensis* is endemic to the northern Western Ghats in Maharashtra, India, typically inhabiting rocky outcrops at elevations between 600 and 1,400 meters.
